findings.issue: OpenMath drops the hypothesis that A and B are square of the same order (and the field K). With matrix_mul / identity_matrix (size fixed by context) it asserts AB=I -> BA=I for arbitrary rectangular A,B, which is exactly the false claim used as the card's own hard_negative; a different (false) theorem gets the identical OpenMath.

findings.issue: In the OpenMath n is only tied to dim V; the families mu and v are not required to have n members. For an injective family with m<n members the conclusion (a basis b indexed like mu with f b_i = mu_i b_i) is false, so the OpenMath states a false generalisation; the Lean target uses Fin n for mu and v.

findings.issue: (finite_set v) is applied to the family v, conflating a finite index set with a finite set of values; the index set of c and of the inner forall (i) is never stated, so OpenMath cannot distinguish 'finite family' from 'family with finitely many distinct values'. The bound variable n never occurs in the body: the OpenMath quantifies over any linearly independent family v (no length n, no ordered index), whereas the Lean target is for v : Fin n -> E. Tie n to the family size.

findings.issue: hard_negative reason (v_1=v_2=1, n=2 gives product 2) is not a counterexample in characteristic 2, where v_j-v_i = v_j+v_i and the false formula coincides with the true one; the claim is over arbitrary fields so the reason must fix K=Q. OpenMath uses the ad-hoc symbol vandermonde_difference_product (used only in this card) for prod_{i<j}(v_j-v_i); a built-in product over index pairs would be reusable; also K and n are not bound.

hard_negative.statement: ファンデルモンドの行列式はΠ_{i<j}(v_i+v_j)である。
hard_negative.reason: 有理数体では成り立たない。n=2, v=(1,2)とすると行列式は2-1=1だが、積は1+2=3である。標数2では$v_j-v_i=v_j+v_i$となり両者は一致するので、反例には体を指定する必要がある。

findings.issue: row_addition_product is a card-specific predicate and is reused for the right (column) factor M although its meaning says 'row addition'. Prefer a reusable name such as transvection_product (product of elementary matrices I+c e_ij, i != j) and use it for both factors.

findings.issue: (sum (matrix_order A) (lambda (j) ...)) passes a bare integer as the summation range of arith1.sum, so the index range (0..n vs 1..n) is unspecified, while the Lean target sums over Fin (n+1). Use an explicit integer interval (e.g. interval1 integer interval 1..matrix_order A). Same pattern in cofactor_mismatch_zero.

The statement is the off-diagonal entry of A*adj A = det A * I and the answer just cites adjugate_product (whose answer proves this very fact); it adds nothing a proof would cite separately. OpenMath uses sum over a bare matrix_order (index range unspecified).

Matrix.inv is defined in Mathlib as (det)^-1 * adjugate, so the Lean target is the definition unfolded and is true even without det A != 0 (junk value 0 = 0 at det 0). The hypothesis is harmless but the Lean statement does not itself certify that the right-hand side is an inverse; consider concluding A * ((det A)^-1 • adj A) = 1 and ((det A)^-1 • adj A) * A = 1.

systemic: Two parallel, inconsistent vocabularies for the same concepts: vector_space_over(V,K) vs vector_space(K,V), finite_dim_space vs fd_vector_space, dimension vs dim_of, subspace_of vs subspace_in, basis_family vs is_basis_family, linear_map_between vs linear_map_over, matrix_mul vs op_comp, matrix_vector_mul vs matrix_vector, injective_function vs injective_map, complementary_subspaces vs is_complement, inter vs subspace_inter; advanced cards also write the zero vector/operator/matrix and identity as numerals 0/1 although zero_vector/zero_matrix/identity_matrix exist. Retrieval keys for the same fact will not match across the two domains; unify before publishing.

Determinant/trace/transpose/associativity cards fix `Field K` (OpenMath often omits K and squareness altogether and relies on matrix_det presupposing a square matrix) although the facts hold over commutative rings/semirings; reuse over Z-matrices is blocked and ring_theory already holds the CommRing versions (matrix_unit_iff_det_unit). Only left_inverse_is_right_inverse lost a hypothesis this way.

Finite families are encoded as (finite_set v) / (size v) on the family itself, conflating index type and set of values; the Lean side uses [Fintype ι] where [Finite ι] would be more reusable (Fintype is needed only where Fintype.card or a sum appears).

Junk-value audit is clean: every finrank/rank target carries FiniteDimensional, Fintype or Fin n; no Nat.card; Set.ncard only on finite subsets of Fin n (Sylvester); every inverse/quotient/division (A⁻¹, μ⁻¹, /det A, /4) is guarded by det≠0, μ≠0 or a real field. All hard_negatives checked are genuinely false/different (one with a char-2 gap: vandermonde_det).

Cross-domain overlap: field-case copies of module/comm-ring results already in modules_categories, ring_theory and functional_analysis (isomorphism theorems, tensor universal property, det-unit criterion, Cauchy-Schwarz).
missing_neighbors: Sylvester rank inequality: rank A + rank B ≤ rank(AB) + n (Matrix.rank_mul_le / Sylvester); only the upper bound rank(AB) ≤ min is present.
Rank subadditivity rank(A+B) ≤ rank A + rank B (Matrix.rank_add_le).

Monotone dimension: S ≤ T in a finite-dimensional space gives finrank S ≤ finrank T (Submodule.finrank_mono); injective f gives finrank V ≤ finrank W, surjective gives finrank W ≤ finrank V (LinearMap.finrank_le_finrank_of_injective).
Every spanning set contains a basis / every vector space has a basis (Module.Basis.ofVectorSpace, exists_linearIndependent) which the answers cite informally.
det(A^{-1}) = (det A)^{-1} and det of a conjugate P A P^{-1} (Matrix.det_nonsing_inv, det_conj).
Trace and determinant as sum/product of eigenvalues over an algebraically closed field (Matrix.trace_eq_sum_roots_charpoly, det_eq_prod_roots_charpoly).
Spectral theorem for normal operators over C, and IsSymmetric <-> self-adjoint (LinearMap.IsSymmetric.eigenvectorBasis, IsSelfAdjoint).

Orthogonal projection facts: starProjection is idempotent, self-adjoint, lands in S, and x - Px ∈ Sᗮ (Submodule.starProjection_apply_mem, IsStarProjection); Bessel inequality for orthonormal families.
Real case ker(AᵀA) = ker A and rank(AᵀA) = rank A (Matrix.rank_transpose_mul_self).
Commuting diagonalizable operators are simultaneously diagonalizable (LinearMap.IsSymmetric.iSup_iInf_eq_top_of_commute / Module.End.iSup_iInf_maxGenEigenspace_eq_top_of_forall_mapsTo).
Complex Schur / triangularisation: every operator on a nonzero finite-dimensional space over an algebraically closed field has a basis in which it is upper triangular.

Dimension of a generalised eigenspace equals the algebraic multiplicity (root multiplicity in charpoly); Fintype-free finiteness of one basis given another finite basis (Module.Basis.finite_index_of_rank_lt_aleph0).
